questions.prompt: What does this code print, in order?
options: `Main continues`, `Worker started`, `Worker done`
`Worker started`, `Main continues`, `Worker done`
`Worker started`, `Worker done`, `Main continues`
`Main continues` only, because the worker is still sleeping
questions.explanation: `Join()` blocks the calling thread until the target thread terminates, so `Main continues` is printed only after the worker has printed both of its lines.

questions.prompt: What happens if you call `Thread.Abort()` in .NET Core / .NET 5+?
options: The target thread stops immediately and safely
It throws a `PlatformNotSupportedException`
It pauses the thread until `Interrupt()` is called
It marks the thread as a background thread
questions.explanation: `Abort()` is obsolete and not supported in .NET Core / .NET 5+, where it throws `PlatformNotSupportedException`; use cooperative cancellation instead.

questions.prompt: You start a thread with `new Thread(new ParameterizedThreadStart(PrintWithParameter))` and `t2.Start("Aman")`. What must `PrintWithParameter` look like?
options: It must take one `string` parameter
It must take no parameters and read the value from a field
It must return the value it was given
It must take one `object` parameter and cast it if needed
questions.explanation: With `ParameterizedThreadStart` the method must accept one `object` parameter; you cast it inside the method if you expect a specific type. A lambda that captures variables avoids the cast.

source.section: #### 2) Thread Running a Method With Parameters

questions.prompt: A worker thread has `IsBackground = true` and is still running when `Main` returns. What happens?
options: The CLR ends the process and stops the worker mid-execution
The process stays alive until the worker finishes
The worker is moved to the thread pool and keeps running
`Main` blocks automatically until the worker calls `Join()`
questions.explanation: Background threads don't keep the process alive: when all foreground threads end, the CLR terminates the process, so the worker's remaining work or cleanup may be incomplete.

questions.prompt: You call `t.Interrupt()` while thread `t` is running normally and not blocked. What happens?
options: The thread is killed at once
Nothing; the call is ignored for running threads
The request is remembered and the exception is thrown when the thread next blocks
The thread throws `ThreadInterruptedException` immediately, wherever it is
questions.explanation: `Interrupt()` doesn't kill a thread. If the thread isn't blocked, the request is remembered and the exception is thrown the next time it enters a blocking call such as `Sleep` or `Join`.
